name: Lynnfield
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Lynnfield, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Lynnfield, MA: Bright Night and Santa at MarketStreet, a free community skate, ornament painting and the Town Common tree lighting.
lede: Lynnfield celebrates Christmas in two places: the historic Town Common, where the Recreation Department throws its Tree Lighting and Whobilation, and MarketStreet, where Santa lights the tree at Bright Night beside an outdoor skating rink.
celebrates: On the Town Common, Lynnfield Recreation hosts the Tree Lighting and Whobilation, a Grinch themed afternoon with games from the Lynnfield Mothers' Group, Girl Scouts and Boy Scouts, face painting, cookies, a library storytime and caroling led by Lynnfield High School singers before the tree is lit. The Recreation Department also publishes a Light Up Lynnfield map of decorated houses to tour after dark and has added a gingerbread house contest. Across town, MarketStreet holds its annual Bright Night tree lighting with Santa, and The SBLI Rink offers outdoor skating all winter.
lastyear: On December 6, 2025, Lynnfield Recreation's Tree Lighting: A Whobilation Celebration filled the Town Common, and the Local Headline News reported that it drew hundreds. The Lynnfield High School Tri-M Music Honor Society, the Chamber Singers and Lynnfield Girl Scouts sang Let It Snow for the crowd. A few days later the Lynnfield Weekly News announced that Light Up Lynnfield was back, with a holiday map of decorated homes and a reminder to visit in the evening when the lights are on.
facts: The tree lighting happens beside one of the oldest buildings around Boston. The Lynnfield Meeting House on the Common dates to 1714 and is thought to be the third oldest Puritan meeting house in New England still standing on its original green. It is older than the Old South Meeting House, Faneuil Hall and King's Chapel in Boston. Over the years it served as a church, town hall, school and fire station, and the old fire alarm bell has sat on a granite block on the Common since 1964.
trains: Lynnfield has no MBTA Commuter Rail station of its own. The closest stop is Wakefield station at 225 North Avenue on the Haverhill Line, with trains to North Station in Boston. For a holiday train ride, Edaville in Carver runs its Holiday Express through Christmas lights. In Lowell, the National Streetcar Museum has hands-on streetcar exhibits for kids, and the Boston and Maine Railroad Historical Society displays steam locomotive No. 410 and a combine car on Dutton Street.

traditions: Lynnfield Recreation's Grinch themed afternoon on the Town Common ends with the town tree lighting.
MarketStreet's annual tree lighting in Market Square comes with crafts, music and Santa, who lights the tree.
The Recreation Department maps the town's best decorated houses so families can plan a lights tour by car or on foot.
Families build houses at home, and the entries go on display at Centre Congregational Church during the tree lighting.
MarketStreet's outdoor rink opens every winter with daily public skating.
Lynnfield High School's Chamber Singers and Tri-M Music Honor Society lead the town in carols at the tree lighting.
kidfact: The big bell sitting on a granite block on Lynnfield Common used to be the town's fire alarm, rung from the old Meeting House when it was a fire station.
faq: It is the nickname for Lynnfield Recreation's annual Tree Lighting and Whobilation on the Town Common, borrowed from the Grinch story. Past years have included games from the Lynnfield Mothers' Group and the Scouts, face painting, cookies, a visit from the Grinch, storytime at the library and caroling by Lynnfield High School singers, with the tree lit at the end.
Where is the Lynnfield town Christmas tree?

The town tree stands on the Town Common in Lynnfield Center, next to the 1714 Meeting House at 617 Main Street, close to the Lynnfield Public Library at 18 Summer Street. Lynnfield Recreation runs the lighting there each December. Past celebrations have included storytime at the library, and this year's gingerbread contest entries go on display at Centre Congregational Church.
Is there ice skating in Lynnfield at Christmas?

Yes. The SBLI Rink at MarketStreet is an outdoor rink that opens in mid November and runs into late February. MarketStreet lists admission at $13, or $20 with skate rentals, and children under 3 skate free. Every skater needs a signed waiver, which can be completed online, and hours depend on the weather.

Light Up Lynnfield is the Recreation Department's holiday lights showcase and map. Residents sign up their decorated houses, and the department shares a map so families can plan a route by car or on foot. The Recreation Department suggests going in the evening, staying a safe distance from private property and following local traffic rules.
Does Lynnfield have a train station?

No. Lynnfield has no MBTA Commuter Rail stop. The nearest stop is Wakefield station at 225 North Avenue on the Haverhill Line, with trains to North Station in Boston. From North Station it is easy to reach the downtown Boston Christmas events covered on our Boston page.
